summary: Fixed the measured live-operation failure from the B384 canonical bridge: eight near-simultaneous review_ready events on one origin thread produced one inflight plus seven pending single-item callbacks (up to eight separate Codex turns), and the then-short App Server timeout caused dead letters on long CEO review turns. Added AITools/taskdb.py::callback_batches -- a durable batch table keyed by a fresh batch_id assigned once at formation time and persisted on every member callback_outbox row. claim_pending_callback_batch atomically coalesces every currently-unassigned pending row for ONE origin_thread_id (bounded, DEFAULT_CALLBACK_BATCH_MAX_MEMBERS=25) into one leased batch: never spans threads, never two inflight batches for the same thread, membership fixed at formation and never re-scanned on restart/lease-reclaim (only re-pruned for staleness via the existing B384 _task_still_in_matching_terminal_state before every (re-)lease, so a stale member can never reach an App Server turn and an event arriving mid-turn simply waits for the next batch). mark_batch_delivered/requeue_batch/mark_batch_dead_letter transition every member of a batch together via a bulk UPDATE scoped to state='inflight' -- exactly-once terminal disposition per member, never a partial delivery. callback_bridge.py::CallbackBridge now claims/delivers/finalizes one whole batch per run_once()/daemon iteration (_process_batch/deliver_callback_batch/build_batch_callback_prompt) instead of one outbox row; the batch prompt lists each member's validated task_id/transition/event id plus the bounded total count and instructs Codex to inspect the complete trusted review queue. App Server timeout/lease/max-batch-members are now CLI/env configurable (--app-server-timeout-seconds/--lease-seconds/--max-batch-members or GEOAI_CALLBACK_APP_SERVER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS/GEOAI_CALLBACK_LEASE_SECONDS/GEOAI_CALLBACK_MAX_BATCH_MEMBERS), validated at startup (validate_lease_and_timeout enforces lease >= timeout + margin, default margin 300s, rejecting an invalid combination immediately -- no 60-second implicit timeout path remains anywhere in the module). Added a coordinator-only, audited dead-letter recovery CLI (taskctl.py callback-recover-dead-letter <outbox_id> --runner codex, gated by the same private coordinator capability as done/reject-review/release-launch/bind-thread) that requeues a dead-lettered row only if its task is STILL in the matching eligible terminal state/episode, else supersedes it. Dashboard/status batch observability required zero dashboard.py code changes: callback_outbox_stats() now nests a 'batches' object (per-state batch counts, current inflight batch member count, oldest pending batch age in seconds, last dead-letter batch member count/error), which flows automatically through the already-existing callback_bridge_health/callback-outbox-status path (verified end-to-end against a real SQLite DB via DashboardProvider, never a full origin_thread_id).

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.bug: mark_batch_delivered and mark_batch_dead_letter originally ran an UNSCOPED `UPDATE callback_outbox SET state=... WHERE batch_id=?` (no `AND state='inflight'` guard). A member pruned as stale by _supersede_stale_batch_members before delivery is marked 'superseded' but keeps its batch_id (for audit/debugging) -- the unscoped UPDATE would incorrectly resurrect that already-superseded row back to 'delivered'/'dead_letter' once its batch finished, contradicting the whole point of the pre-delivery supersede check.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.caught_by: This session's own new test_partial_stale_members_pruned_before_delivery (a batch with one stale + one still-valid member) -- failed with 2 delivered instead of 1 on first run, diagnosed via a standalone repro script, then fixed by adding `AND state='inflight'` to both UPDATE statements (requeue_batch already had this guard).
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.status: FIXED -- re-verified: the same test plus the full suite pass.

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.bug: claim_pending_callback_batch had no guard preventing a SECOND concurrent caller from forming/leasing a SECOND inflight batch for a thread that already had one inflight (undelivered). Reproduced directly: claim batch1 for thread X (leave it inflight, undelivered), seed a new eligible row for the SAME thread X, call claim_pending_callback_batch again -- it formed and leased batch2 for the SAME thread X, i.e. two simultaneous inflight batches for one origin thread. Safety had rested entirely on the operational fact that the daemon/run_once loop is single-process/serial (claim -> synchronously deliver -> claim again), not on any DB-level invariant -- a second bridge instance, a manual `run-once` racing an active `daemon`, or restart overlap could have produced a real parallel-turn-on-busy-thread violation (the exact thing forbidden by this task's own acceptance criteria), with safety only reactively dependent on the real Codex App Server itself correctly reporting 'busy' across two SEPARATE app-server subprocesses -- an assumption never verified.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.caught_by: An independent adversarial verification agent, tasked with re-deriving batching correctness from the code rather than trusting this worker's own summary -- it reproduced the race empirically with a minimal repro script before reporting it.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.fix: claim_pending_callback_batch now computes `busy_threads` (every origin_thread_id with a currently state='inflight' batch) once per claim attempt, immediately after reclaiming expired leases, and excludes those threads from BOTH the pending-batch-resume candidates and the new-batch-formation candidates. A thread's waiting pending rows are simply left unassigned until its inflight batch resolves (delivered/dead-lettered/requeued), at which point the NEXT claim call correctly forms a fresh batch for them. Cross-thread claims remain fully independent and unaffected.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_se.status: FIXED -- re-verified: reproduced-then-fixed with a standalone script, then re-verified in isolation with a race scenario (concurrent-claim blocked for the busy thread, an unrelated thread still claimable independently, the waiting event correctly forms its own batch once the first resolves), and captured as a permanent regression test (test_concurrent_claim_never_forms_a_second_inflight_batch_for_same_thread).

batching_design.schema: AITools/taskdb.py::callback_batches (batch_id PK, origin_thread_id, state, created_at, updated_at, attempts, last_error, lease_id, lease_expires_at, member_count) + callback_outbox.batch_id (idempotent ALTER TABLE migration, _migrate_callback_outbox_add_batch_id_column).
batching_design.claim_pending_callback_batch: BEGIN IMMEDIATE retry loop (mirrors B384's claim_pending_callback structure): reclaims expired-lease inflight batches (state->pending, members revert too); prefers resuming an existing pending batch (FIFO by created_at) over forming a new one; a new batch coalesces every unassigned pending row for the SAME origin_thread_id as the oldest unassigned row, bounded by max_members; every candidate (existing or new) is pruned via _supersede_stale_batch_members immediately before leasing; a fully-pruned batch is marked superseded and the loop retries.
batching_design.why_no_client_user_message_id_column: batch_id itself is already a durable identifier assigned once and persisted -- deterministic_batch_client_user_message_id(batch_id) hashes it directly at delivery time rather than storing a redundant derived column.
batching_design.prompt_shape: build_batch_callback_prompt(members) lists '- task_id=... state=... event_id=... request_id=...' per member (each independently validated via the same _validate_callback_fields used by the single-item build_callback_prompt) plus a '{count} task(s)' header and an instruction to inspect the complete trusted review queue.
batching_design.one_batch_per_thread_never_two_inflight: Enforced at the DB layer (not just by the single-process serial daemon loop): claim_pending_callback_batch computes the set of origin_thread_ids with a currently state=inflight batch on every claim attempt and excludes those threads from both the pending-batch-resume and new-batch-formation candidate queries, so a second concurrent caller (a second bridge instance, a manual run-once racing an active daemon, or restart overlap) can never lease a competing batch for a thread that already has one inflight -- see real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_sessions_own_verification for the exact race this closes.

configurable_timeout_lease.precedence: CLI flag > env var > safe default (DEFAULT_APP_SERVER_TIMEOUT=1800.0, DEFAULT_LEASE_SECONDS=2100, max_batch_members=25).
configurable_timeout_lease.validation: validate_lease_and_timeout() requires lease_seconds > 0, app_server_timeout > 0, and lease_seconds >= app_server_timeout + margin_seconds (default DEFAULT_LEASE_MARGIN_SECONDS=300.0); raises ValueError immediately (main() prints the error and exits 2) rather than starting with an unsafe pair. Production defaults (2100/1800) satisfy this with a 300s margin. The margin itself is NOT exposed via CLI/env -- only CallbackBridge's constructor accepts an explicit lease_margin_seconds override, a deliberate, visible test/dev-only escape hatch that the production CLI path never exposes.
configurable_timeout_lease.no_60_second_implicit_path: Verified by test_no_hardcoded_60_second_timeout_default: DEFAULT_APP_SERVER_TIMEOUT != 60, and AppServerClient's own default timeout equals DEFAULT_APP_SERVER_TIMEOUT, not a separate hardcoded 60.

dead_letter_recovery.gate: _require_coordinator (same private 0600-token-file capability as done/reject-review/release-launch/bind-thread) -- verified rejected with a non-coordinator token (test_callback_recover_dead_letter_cli_requires_coordinator_capability).
dead_letter_recovery.logic: taskdb.recover_dead_letter_row: requeues (state->pending, batch_id cleared so it forms a fresh batch, attempts/lease reset) only if the task is STILL in the matching eligible terminal state/episode (via the same _task_still_in_matching_terminal_state check batching itself uses); otherwise supersedes. Every outcome is recorded on the task's own event log (callback_dead_letter_recovered / callback_dead_letter_superseded).
